correctness.rationale: After scalar normalization, the standard extremal-measure equality criterion gives unit coefficient moduli and flat Fourier modulus. Finite cyclic autocorrelation reduces flatness exactly to C1=C2=0 and conjugates. The unit-triangle lemma parametrizes every C1 solution; C2 then forces t^5=omega^q. Removing the threefold parametrization redundancy yields precisely two fifth-root families. Direct substitution proves sufficiency. The exact verifier checks the resulting finite exponent parametrization.

originality.rationale: The new statement classifies all coefficient equality cases on a support whose extremality is classical. The 1981 source classifies supports, while the 2019 source gives the general flatness criterion, completely classifies a different three-point example, and gives only sample witnesses for this four-point example. The exhaustive analytic classification here is therefore not implied by the inspected statements.
residual_risks: Older sequence-design, perfect-sequence, or complex weighing-matrix literature may encode the same classification under different terminology.
The 1981 paper predates modern electronic indexing; its support theorem was inspected, but an uncatalogued equality-case note cannot be ruled out by search alone.

value.rationale: The fixed support is a classical minimal nontrivial example where later literature explicitly displays different extremal measures. Completing the equality cases into ten normalized solutions and two modulation orbits resolves that observed nonuniqueness structurally and gives a reusable autocorrelation argument, rather than merely recomputing the known Sidon constant.
